reviews.title: Noticeable performance boost in HP Envy after upgrade
reviews.comment: I installed this in my HP Envy laptop as a RAM upgrade, and the difference was immediate. Before the upgrade, the system would slow down with multiple applications open. After installing this, overall performance improved noticeably. Things like multitasking, opening applications, and general responsiveness are much smoother. Installation was straightforward. It was recognized right away with no compatibility issues. So far, it’s been stable with no crashes or performance problems. Pros Immediate improvement in system performance Easy installation No compatibility issues in my HP Envy Stable under normal use Cons None so far Bottom Line If you’re upgrading RAM in a compatible laptop, this is a solid option that delivers a noticeable performance improvement.
reviews.author: Mike Walker

reviews.title: Paired well with 16gb stick from different brand
reviews.comment: Added to my older laptop that had an open RAM slot. Made sure all the specs line up and it was compatible. It works like a charm and is much better than paying twice as much for a matching pair. The first boot up after install gives you a black screen for about 30-60 seconds while things get familiar, then its good to go. If you've never installed ram before or fiddled with your PC internals, watch tutorials so that you don't mess up your computer.

reviews.title: The Finest Laptop RAM on the Market for non-XMP boards/BIOS
reviews.comment: Starting with specifics, I installed this RAM on a ASUS TUF F17 Series Laptop - FX706HE. Installation takes about 1-2 minutes, or however fast you can unscrew the bottom of your Laptop and replace two SODIMMs. I decided to go with the 64GB Kit. Some people may think that this is too much RAM, but it's nearly 2023, and I prescribe to the philosophy that my computer works for me, not the other way around. I should not be forced to close tabs or programs to free up RAM to play games. I should also not have to rely on a Page File in case my RAM gets capped. When it comes to Laptop SODIMM RAM, you're probably not going to find much faster than CL22, even at 8GB, unless it uses XMP. Unfortunately, a lot of Laptop BIOS's, including the one for my ASUS TUF Series, does not have this feature. Now, I don't know if it's specifically a mainboard or BIOS issue where I could have enabled the feature by completely flushing my BIOS - but that seemed like a really stupid and dangerous idea where I would end up bricking my laptop. When I initially realized this, I just let out a sigh, and had to accept that my laptop would not enable XMP, or higher voltage RAM. So, in my humble opinion, this is your best option for Laptops that do not have XMP. It's plug-and-play option (which basically means it's default setting) allows you to get XMP speeds, without the use of XMP. Now, we're not talking about going from CL22 to CL16 here - it's a modest reduction to CL20 - but when your choices are limited, you take what you can get. At the default CL20, it still maintains 3200MHz. The 64GB Kit is both Dual Channel and Dual Rank. I immediately noticed performance gains in more RAM heavy games, like Star Citizen. And, FYI, going from Single Rank to Dual Rank doesn't give you some magical 30% FPS increase with all games across the board, like some people claim. But, the I'm sure that the combined effect of a lower CL, higher capacity, and dual ranking all adds to the overall performance impact. I'll toss in some CPU-Z screenshots for those interested in the finer details. Overall, unless the hardware dies on me within a short amount of time, 5 Stars. It's nice to see a brand like Kingston providing a RAM solution that solves an issue that affects more users than I originally realize.
reviews.author: RW
